title: SLO-driven eval gating and quantization handoff playbook
author: Marisol Chen
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines an SLO-driven gating strategy for automated evaluation pipelines and prescribes the operational handoff for quantized model artifacts into shadow and production-serving lanes. The goal is to prevent quantization or performance regressions from reaching customers while enabling fast, reproducible promotion for models that meet both quality and latency/cost objectives.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all model promotions that include a quantized artifact (int8, 4-bit, hybrid-mixed precision) or runtime kernel/packing changes.
- Covers: automated eval gates (pre-promotion), manual triage escalation, shadow deployment gating, and final rollout controls.
- Excludes security-only certification (handled by security-and-compliance).

Definitions:
- Eval Gate: A checkpoint in the CI/eval pipeline that requires pass/fail criteria before artifacts move downstream.
- Promotion Candidate: A model version + quant artifact produced by the quantization pipeline.
- Shadow Lane: Isolated serving environment with production-like traffic for fidelity and performance validation.
- Delta SLO: The allowed deviation from baseline for a given metric (e.g., -1.5% mean accuracy).

SLO matrix (examples):
| Metric                        | Baseline (prod model) | Allowed Delta (gate) | Action on breach       | Monitoring source           |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------|----------------------|-------------------------|-----------------------------|
| Mean ROUGE / BLEU / F1        | 0.78                  | -0.015               | Block promotion        | eval-summaries, slices API  |
| Latency P95 (ms)              | 180                   | +40ms                | Block promotion        | perf-traces, runtime-metrics|
| Token cost / 1k tokens (USD)  | 0.032                 | +10%                 | Warn + require signoff    | cost-ledger                 |
| Response Stability Index (RSI)| 0.94                  | -0.02                | Block promotion        | stability-service           |
| Functioncall success rate     | 99.6%                 | -0.5%                | Manual triage            | functioncall-metrics       |

Gating rules (high-level):
1. Unit-level evals (fast): run on PR; must pass regression sentinel tests and tokenization sanity checks. Failure: block PR merge.
2. Slice-level evals (medium): run in CI-eval cluster against prioritized slice set (latency-sensitive, high-value intents). Failure: create regression ticket; require owner triage and signoff to proceed to shadow.
3. Shadow smoke (slow): promote candidate to shadow lane with 1% production traffic multiplexed for 24–72 hours. Monitor SLOs; any block-level metric breach for > 30 minutes triggers automatic demotion.
4. Final rollout: if shadow passes, schedule staggered rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with canary hold windows and automatic rollback on live regressions.

Quantization handoff checklist (artifact producer responsibilities):
- Produce deterministic artifact bundle: model.card, quant.metadata.json, kernel-config.yml, and checksums.
- Attach eval manifests: commit hash for eval harness, slice-set id, random seeds used, and perf seed trace.
- Run local safety checks: tokenization parity, functioncall smoke, and small-sample coherence tests.
- Upload artifact to artifact repo with tag: quant/<model>-<version>-<quant-profile>-<date>. Example: quant/gpt-style-1.4-q4_1-20260112

Handoff YAML (example):
---
artifact_tag: "quant/gpt-style-1.4-q4_1-20260112"
producer: "quant-team/autoquant-v2"
eval_manifest: "evals/manifest/2026-01-10-quick.json"
required_gates:
  - unit_sentinels
  - slice_regressions
  - shadow_smoke
promotion_policy:
  shadow_duration_hours: 48
  canary_steps: [5, 25, 100]
  rollback_on: [response_stability_index, p95_latency, mean_fidelity]
---

Operational runbook: step-by-step
1) Submit artifact: producer uploads artifact and triggers "eval-harness run" with tag.
   CLI: eval-harness run --artifact quant/gpt-style-1.4-q4_1-20260112 --slices priority-slice-set --parallel 12
2) Fast gate: unit tests and sentinel checks run (target: < 30 minutes). If any sentinel fails, pipeline creates an automated regression incident and marks the artifact failed.
3) Slice gate: run full slice suite (target: 2–6 hours). Summary report posted to /evals/reports/<artifact_tag>.
4) If slice gate passes, orchestrator triggers shadow promotion job. Shadow config: 1% traffic, 48h, telemetry piped to shadow namespace. 
5) Monitoring and alerting: paging thresholds are configured in monitoring-playbooks:
   - RSI drop >= 0.02 sustained for 30m -> P1 on-call page
   - Latency P95 exceed baseline + 40ms for 4 consecutive 5m windows -> P1
   - Token cost > baseline + 15% for 1h -> SRE on-call.
6) Failures during shadow: run quick rollback script and open triage.
   CLI: eval-harness rollback --shadow quant/gpt-style-1.4-q4_1-20260112 --reason "p95_latency"
7) After successful shadow, schedule canary rollout with annotated ticket linking eval report, perf traces, and signoffs.

Triage decision tree (condensed):
- Block-level metric breach? -> Immediate demotion and assign regression-owner -> create incident -> run bisect (if multiple quant profiles) -> if root cause is quant param, attempt localized re-quant or adjust kernel config.
- Cost regression only? -> Flag for product + finance review; require explicit product signoff to proceed.
- Small quality delta within allowed but customer-sensitive slice affected? -> Run targeted human review on slice, consider per-tenant hold.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Quantization team: produce artifacts, include metadata, respond to quant-specific failures.
- Applied ML / Eval team: owns eval manifests, slice prioritization, and gate automation.
- SRE: owns rollout orchestration, shadow routing, and emergency rollback tooling.
- Product owner: approves cost deviations and tenant-risk signoffs.

Metrics to publish with every promotion candidate (minimum):
- eval_summary_url (string)
- delta_metrics: {"rsi": "-0.006", "p95_latency_ms": "+12"} (as JSON blob in report)
- perf_trace_id
- artifact_checksums

Common failure modes and remediations:
- Non-deterministic eval results across seeds: increase sample seeds to 10 and run multi-seed aggregator; check for tokenization nondeterminism.
- Latency regression only on long contexts: add context-limited micro-bench and consider KV cache tuning or kernel selection override.
- Functioncall mismatch after quantization: run functioncall-priming harness and verify call-signature fidelity; if failing, mark quant profile as unsuited.

Fast rollback checklist (emergency):
1. Set routing to previous stable artifact: routingctl set-default <service> --artifact <stable-tag>
2. Pause ongoing shadow/canary promotions.
3. Open incident with tags: quant, regression, auto-rollback.
4. Triage owner runs bisect on quant parameter set and uploads findings to incident.

Promotion signoff template (required in ticket):
- Artifact tag:
- Eval run id and link:
- Shadow duration and traffic: (hours, %)
- Key delta metrics (table): RSI, P95 latency, top-5 slice regressions
- Risk notes and mitigation plan:
- Approvals: quant lead, applied-ml lead, SRE lead, product manager

Appendix: example eval-harness commands and useful endpoints
- Start controlled eval: eval-harness run --artifact <tag> --slices <slice-set> --output /evals/reports/<tag>.json
- Promote to shadow: eval-orchestrator promote --artifact <tag> --lane shadow --traffic 1% --duration 48h
- Query stability: curl -s "https://monitoring.internal/api/v1/slices/<slice-id>/stability?artifact=<tag>"

References and related policies:

- Quant safety baseline: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024
- Shadow deployment pattern: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/shadow-deployments
